probe: Can a SessionStart hook show a notice to the user, or only to the model?
harness: Claude Code 2.1.276, headless (-p, stream-json), model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
method: Throwaway git project in the scratchpad with a committed-style .claude/settings.json whose SessionStart hook prints one JSON object: systemMessage carrying token KQ-PROBE-USER-NOTICE, hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext carrying token KQ-PROBE-MODEL-CONTEXT. Prompt: reply OK and repeat any KQ-PROBE token in context.

observed.hook_ran: yes: a system/hook_response event for SessionStart:startup carries the hook's stdout
observed.additionalContext: reached the model: the reply was 'OK' followed by KQ-PROBE-MODEL-CONTEXT
observed.systemMessage: present only in the hook_response event; the model did not see it. Whether the interactive UI displays it is not observable headlessly

verdict: The model channel (additionalContext) is measured and reliable. The user channel (systemMessage) is unverified in the interactive UI. A notice that must reach the user uses both: systemMessage for the UI, and additionalContext asking the model to tell the user once.
